I don’t have direct access to the web right now, so I can’t pull up *live* headlines for you. However, there are several reliable ways (and even free APIs) to grab fresh stock‑market news yourself: | What you’re looking for | How to get it | |-------------------------|---------------| | **General market headlines** | • [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/markets)
• Bloomberg Market News
• Yahoo! Finance “Markets” tab | | **Company‑specific news** | • Google Search `"" news`
• Finance sites’ company pages (e.g., Apple – https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL)` | | **Programmatic retrieval** | • Finnhub.io’s `/stock/news` endpoint
• AlphaVantage’s `NEWS_SENTIMENT` feed (limited free tier)
• YFinance library (`yfinance.Ticker(ticker).news`) | --- ### Quick demo: Pulling news for a ticker with Finnhub ```python import os import requests API_KEY = os.getenv("FINNHUB_APIKEY") # sign up at finnhub.co → get your key BASE_URL = "https://finnhub.io/api/v1" def get_stock_news(symbol: str, limit: int = 5): """ Returns the most recent headline articles for a given symbol. Parameters: symbol : str # Stock ticker (e.g., "AAPL") limit : int # Number of top stories to return Output: List of dicts containing title, source, datetime, URL, summary """ url = f"{BASE_URL}/stock/news" params = { "symbol": symbol.upper(), "token" : API_KEY, "limit" : limit } resp = requests.get(url, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() if __name__ == "__main__": print(get_stock_news("TSLA", 10)) ``` #### Sample JSON response (truncated) ```json [ { "category":"general", "datetime":1715625600, "headline":"Tesla Q2 earnings beat expectations; shares rally", "id":"123456789", "image":"", "related":["TSLA"], "source":"CNBC", "summary":"Tesla reported higher-than-expected quarterly revenue...", "url":"https://www.cnbc.com/.../tesla-q2-results.html" }, ... ] ``` Just replace `"TSLA"` with whatever ticker you care about, set `limit`, and you’ll see the latest headlines. --- ### If you prefer no coding 1. Go to [Finviz](https://finviz.com/) and search for the ticker. 2. Click the “News” tab under the chart. 3. You’ll see all major press releases, analyst reports, and media coverage sorted chronologically. Feel free to let me know a specific ticker or sector you’d like updates on—then I can tailor the query string or script accordingly!
